breakfast.name: Piernik (Polish Gingerbread)
breakfast.description: Traditional Polish gingerbread cake with honey and spices
breakfast.notes: Best if aged a few days for flavors to develop
breakfast.fun_fact: Polish piernik has been made for centuries and varies by region

lunch.name: Bigos (Hunter's Stew)
lunch.description: Polish stew with sauerkraut, fresh cabbage, and multiple meats that improves with time
instructions: Brown meats in pot, set aside
Can simmer longer for deeper flavor
Better the next day after flavors meld
lunch.notes: Traditionally made in large batches and eaten over several days
lunch.fun_fact: Bigos was the favorite dish of Polish hunters and the national stew of Poland

dinner.name: Pierogi (Filled Dumplings)
dinner.description: Polish dumplings with various fillings, served with sour cream and caramelized onions
instructions: Make dough with flour, water, egg, salt
Mix mashed potatoes with cheese for filling
Place filling on circle, fold, seal edges
Boil until dumplings float plus 2 minutes
Serve with caramelized onions and sour cream
dinner.notes: Fillings vary: potato-cheese, sauerkraut, mushroom, plum
dinner.fun_fact: Pierogi are so important to Polish culture that there's an annual Festival of Pierogi

snacks.name: Żurek (Sour Rye Soup)
snacks.description: Traditional sour rye soup with ham and potatoes
instructions: Let rye flour ferment in water for 2-3 days (or use store-bought sour rye starter)
Add broth, strained rye liquid, potatoes, ham
Serve with dollop of sour cream
snacks.notes: The fermented rye base is key to authentic flavor
snacks.fun_fact: Żurek is traditionally served on Easter Monday in Poland
alternatives: Skip fermentation and use rye starter

desserts.name: Sernik (Polish Cheesecake)
desserts.description: Tall, airy Polish cheesecake with fluffy texture
instructions: Make crust, press in springform pan
Beat yolks with sugar until pale
Mix cheese, yolks, vanilla, lemon zest
Gently fold in egg whites in batches
Cool completely in oven with door cracked
desserts.notes: The high eggs-to-cheese ratio makes it fluffy, not dense
desserts.fun_fact: Polish sernik is taller and airier than American cheesecake

nonAlcoholicDrinks.name: Kompot (Fruit Compote)
nonAlcoholicDrinks.description: Polish sweet fruit drink made from fresh or dried fruits
ingredients: 2 cups mixed fresh fruit (apples, plums, berries)
instructions: Bring water and sugar to boil
nonAlcoholicDrinks.notes: Can be made with dried fruit for off-season
nonAlcoholicDrinks.fun_fact: Kompot is a staple at Polish family meals and celebrations

alcoholicDrinks.name: Polish Vodka
alcoholicDrinks.description: Clear, high-proof Polish spirit, often served ice-cold as shot
ingredients: Polish vodka (e.g., Żubrówka, Zubrowka Bison Grass)
instructions: Often followed by pickle juice chaser
alcoholicDrinks.notes: Some varieties include bison grass or other infusions
alcoholicDrinks.fun_fact: Poland is famous for vodka production and has been since the 15th century
